title: 1979 AHSME Problem 16
statement: A circle with area \(A_1\) is contained in the interior of a larger circle with area \(A_1+A_2.\) If the radius of the larger circle is \(3,\) and if \(A_1,\) \(A_2,\) \(A_1+A_2\) is an arithmetic progression, then the radius of the smaller circle is

solutions.text:
The progression condition gives \[ 2A_2=A_1+(A_1+A_2), \] so \(A_2=2A_1.\) Hence the larger area is \(3A_1=9\pi,\) and \(A_1=3\pi.\) If the smaller radius is \(r,\) then \(\pi r^2=3\pi,\) so \(r=\sqrt3.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Use the middle-term condition for the three areas in arithmetic progression
Express the larger circle’s area as a multiple of \(A_1\)
